why: I checked all five expect lines and their proofs. Each one is a `run` proof with concrete commands that work in a checkout of the PR head. Lines 1, 2 and 4 make a temp file, run `node src/app.js` on it, and check the exit code, stdout and stderr ("grep -qF \"$F\" $d/err", "grep -q 'line 3'", "listening on 9000"). Line 3 imports loadConfig and checks that it prints `THREW true` rather than `RETURNED`. Line 5 runs `npm test` at the head, then puts back src/ from base commit 799ce33 and runs the tests again. That commit already exists before merge, so this is a valid check before merge too. Each line gives one clear yes or no answer. None of them needs a release, a deploy, a published page or anything else that only exists after merge. So the criterion holds for the whole output.
